correctness.rationale: The proof gives a bijective decomposition of every fixed-point-free endomorphism of \(X\oplus A_r\). A fixed-point-free map cannot send a point of \(X\) to a new maximum, because monotonicity would then force that maximum to be fixed. After restricting to \(g\in\operatorname{Fpf}(X)\), each new maximum has exactly \(u(g)\) admissible images in \(X\) and \(r-1\) admissible new maxima, independently. The converse extension is checked directly. The packaged exhaustive verifier independently confirms all labeled \(X\) through four points for \(r=2\), and through three points for \(r=3\); the computation is explicitly limited to regression testing.

value.rationale: The result attaches an exact, self-contained invariant to a standard finite-topology construction rather than to an arbitrary finite slice. For the non-Hausdorff suspension it refines a yes/no fixed-point-property statement to a complete count, and it identifies the precise statistic \(u(g)\) controlling multiplicity. This gives a reusable recurrence whenever fixed-point-free maps of the base and their image upper bounds are understood, while keeping the limits explicit.
